How to make a YouTube QR code

A YouTube QR code is a normal QR code that stores a YouTube link.

  1. Open the video, channel or playlist on YouTube and use Share to copy the link.
  2. Paste the link into the field above.
  3. Pick colors, add a logo if you like, and choose a frame such as "Watch now".
  4. Download the PNG for screens or the SVG for print.
  5. Scan the finished code with a phone and check that it opens the right page.

Which YouTube link should you use?

Different links do different jobs. Choose the one that matches what you want people to do.

LinkWhat the scanner seesGood for
A single videoThat videoProduct demos, tutorials, event recaps, music videos
A channel linkYour channel pageBuilding subscribers from flyers and packaging
A playlist linkA list of videos in orderCourses, series, how-to sets
A link with a start timeA video that starts at a chosen secondSkipping intros, jumping to the useful part
A YouTube ShortA vertical videoShort promos and social content

Getting subscribers with a channel QR code

For a channel, use your channel URL, which usually looks like youtube.com/@yourname. Some creators add a subscribe prompt to the end of the link. Test any modified link on a phone before printing, because YouTube may change how links behave.

Give people a reason to scan, for example "Scan for the full tutorial", rather than a bare code.

Tips for YouTube QR codes

A few habits make video codes work better.

  • Use links you control. If a video is deleted or made private, the code stops working.
  • Make the video worth it. People scan when they expect something short and useful.
  • Think about mobile data. On posters in places with weak signal, a short video loads better.
  • Keep the code at least about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, larger for anything scanned from a distance.
  • Do not put a QR code on a video that is the destination itself. On-screen codes can be hard to scan at video size.
